Health can’t wait.

Alan exists to end the wait.

It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

About the Growth team

Growth Marketing at Alan covers a broad range of opportunities, including acquisition, segment and market growth, partnerships, content, experimentation, and international expansion.

We are looking for adaptable marketers who can take ownership of a defined growth problem, learn quickly, and evolve as our priorities change.

 

Your mission

As a Growth Marketer, you will independently own an ambiguous but defined Growth problem from diagnosis through execution. You will prioritise the highest-impact actions, coordinate the relevant stakeholders, and connect your work to measurable business outcomes.

Concretely, our team works on missions such as:

  • Developing our channels: scaling paid acquisition, growing visibility in AI search and LLMs like ChatGPT, or growing our strategic partnerships

  • Crafting the go-to-market strategy for our different segments (e.g. retirees, freelancers, companies,...)

  • Producing performance creatives with AI workflows to create assets at scale

 

What you will do

  • Independently own an ambiguous but defined Growth problem from diagnosis through execution.

  • Prioritise high-impact opportunities and make clear trade-offs.

  • Design and run experiments, campaigns, or programmes end to end.

  • Coordinate the relevant stakeholders and move initiatives forward with limited direction.

  • Use business and performance data to make decisions and establish a clear learning loop.

  • Adapt your approach based on results, customer insight, and feedback.

  • Connect your work to measurable business outcomes.

What we are looking for

  • Experience owning a meaningful Growth, acquisition, segment, market, or related Marketing scope.

  • Strong problem-framing, prioritisation, and experimentation skills.

  • Ability to make decisions based on evidence and business impact.

  • Hands-on execution combined with an understanding of adjacent teams and activities.

  • Ability to work with limited direction in an ambiguous environment.

  • Clear communication and constructive stakeholder management.

  • Curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to expand your scope over time.

  • Advanced written and verbal communication skills in English

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the B1-C1 level range.

 

🎯 Important note: we hire people, not roles.

jobs.description:
English to German (Switzerland) Review Lead for UI, Marketing & Product Content

About Welo Global 

Welo Global is a leader in multilingual AI, technology, and content solutions serving over 2,000 clients in 300 languages. The company combines globally scaled multilingual infrastructure, including a network of over 500,000 linguists and domain experts, with advanced NLP, computational linguistics, and best-in-class compliance backed by seven ISO certifications. Welo Global’s five brands—Welocalize (multilingual content and localization services for global enterprises), Park IP (intellectual property and patent translation services for law firms and corporate legal teams), Welo Life Sciences (regulated language and compliance-aligned content solutions for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device organizations), Adapt (multilingual performance-led digital marketing agency), and Welo Data (multilingual data generation, evaluation, and human data infrastructure for AI systems)—serve distinct customer segments with purpose-built expertise, fit-for-purpose solutions, and supporting technology. weloglobal.com  


The Role 

We are seeking an experienced English into German (Switzerland) Review Lead to serve as the language quality owner and primary client-facing linguistic expert for a leading global technology client. 

You will own the locale’s interpretation of the client’s quality standards and make sure that the Post-Editing Lead, Post Editors, and Reviewers all work to the same shared understanding of “good”. You will be the main point of contact for the client’s Language Manager on quality discussions, arbitration, and escalations, and you will drive consistency, quality governance, and continuous improvement across UI, marketing, product, informational, legal, and support content. 

Project Details 

- Location: Remote (based in one of the approved countries below)
- Expected volume: Approximately 24 hours per month
- Employment type: Freelance / Independent Contract
- Task type: Language Lead Support
- Content types: UI, Marketing, Informational, Legal, Product, Support
- Language pair: English into German from Switzerland

What You Will Do 

-Analyse requirements: Review every style guide and glossary update, assess which quality categories and content types it affects, and record the changes. Track what the client’s Language Manager actually corrects and says in calibration and quality calls, not only what is written down.
-Relay expectations: Run regular alignment roundtables with the language community and publish a structured monthly quality digest covering performance, priority improvement areas, style guide updates, and notable errors and arbitration outcomes.
-Manage review quality actively: Coach Reviewers one-to-one using specific examples, run shadowing sessions, and deliver training built from real alignment data.
-Improve the standard: Turn recurring justification patterns into well-reasoned style guide proposals, and share cross-locale patterns with the Welocalize Quality Manager.
-Maintain alignment with the client: Treat Language Manager decisions as the standard, raise concerns with evidence at the right forum, and aim for fewer surprises over time.

What You Will Own

-The locale’s review service score, including RQE audit and alignment performance
-The community’s shared understanding of quality 
-The integrity of the arbitration record, ensuring that every arbitration sent to the client is valid and well-evidenced
-The working relationship with the client’s Language Manager, including clarifications, escalations, and expectation tracking

Requirements

- Experience: 3 to 5+ years in Localization Quality Assurance (LQA), Senior Language Lead, or Quality Governance roles
- Client and stakeholder management: Direct experience as the primary point of contact for client Language Managers, managing formal arbitration or escalation processes, and facilitating conflict resolution
- Quality audit frameworks: Deep, practical experience with localization evaluation frameworks, including RQE, LQE, error rubrics, and severity mapping
- Style guide and expectation analysis: Ability to analyse style guide changes, identify implicit client expectations, and map tolerance by content type (for example, Marketing vs. Legal vs. UI)
- Meeting facilitation: Hands-on experience with one-to-one coaching, shadowing sessions, alignment roundtables, and structured monthly quality reporting
- Analytical approach: Skill in tracking error concentrations, severity drift, and alignment scores, and in converting justification patterns into style guide improvements
- Language: Native-level German (Switzerland) and professional-level English
- Preferred: Prior experience supporting major technology localization programs and working with calibration or alignment tools

Additional Key Information 

- Successful candidates will be provided with a dedicated device for project work.
- A background check is required as part of onboarding.
- Candidates must be physically located in one of the approved countries.

Approved countries: Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Egypt, El Salvador, Finland, France, Germany, Ghana, Greece, Guatemala, Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Lithuania, Malaysia, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Nigeria, Norway, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States and Vietnam.  

Why Join Us 

This role offers a long-term partnership with global teams on high-visibility products. You will benefit from steady project volume, comprehensive onboarding and ongoing upskilling, and access to established linguistic resources. 

If this sounds like the right opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Security Engineer Senior - GRC
jobs.description:
Security Engineer Senior - GRC

Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

🛡️ The role

Most GRC roles are about keeping auditors happy. This one is about earning our members' trust: every day, they share their diagnoses, their claims and their care with us.

You'll own security governance and risk at Alan end to end. That means one clear framework across our certifications and regulations, which the whole company uses to decide what matters most. You set the direction, make the calls on risk, and help every team own its part.

We just earned our HDS certification, and there's much more to build as we grow from 1M to many millions of members, across more countries and regulators. That includes how we govern AI, which Alan uses across its products and operations.

This is a hands-on senior role. You do the work yourself, mentor the junior GRC engineer we're hiring alongside you, and grow the team over time.

 

🚀 What you'll do

  • Make our security framework a tool for the whole company. You own the full certification cycle (ISO 27001, HDS and those to come), and turn it into something teams use every day to prioritise, not a binder for auditors.

  • Bring the security view on regulation. Legal and Risk own the regulatory relationships. You bring the security answer: what the rules mean for how we protect data, and which controls make it work in practice.

  • Run risk as an ongoing programme. You map and prioritise security risks, including AI risks, turn them into clear treatment plans, and feed them into company-wide risk decisions with the Risk team.

  • Help every team own its risks. You define the controls framework and the standards, while the teams who build and run our systems own the controls. You brief the board and audit committee, and you know which findings need an urgent call and which can wait for the quarterly report.

  • Own incident governance. You triage and escalate incidents, own business continuity and disaster recovery, and shape the security side of our regulatory incident reports.

  • Be a credible partner to engineering. You work with engineering teams early on new designs and spot control gaps (access, encryption, logging) before they ship. You don't need to be an architect, but you can hold the conversation.

     

🏗️ What you'll build

  • One governance model: clear ownership of risks and controls across teams, so security decisions don't bottleneck on one person.

  • A living risk map: prioritised risks that actually drive company and engineering decisions.

  • One compliance backbone: a single control system across our countries and regulators, built to scale.

  • An automated evidence engine: evidence collected straight from engineering systems, so audits run continuously instead of as a quarterly rush.

You'll work closely with Legal, the Data Protection Officer, Internal Audit and Risk, and day to day with engineering and operations teams.

 

⭐ What we're looking for

Your team

You'll join Alan's Corporate team, which brings together our control functions: Risk, Corporate Governance & Internal Control, Legal, Compliance and Security. They share one mission: building what lets Alan operate at scale, safely and responsibly. Within that group, you carry the security governance and risk dimension, working hand in hand with the security engineers who run our infrastructure and platform security, and with a junior GRC engineer we're hiring alongside you. You'll be hands-on every day, building and owning the work yourself. Along the way, you'll mentor the junior engineer and help shape how GRC grows at Alan.

What you bring

  • You want to build and own things yourself, and you enjoy helping someone else grow while you do it.

  • 6+ years in security, with real GRC ownership.

  • You've run a GRC roadmap in a certified or strongly regulated environment (ISO 27001, HDS, SOC 2, or regulated sectors like health, insurance or finance). You're comfortable working with certification auditors, and you can explain what a framework requires and why it makes sense for business teams.

  • You take a stand on risks, and you'd rather close one real risk than write ten policies.

  • You're fluent in French and English.

     

A big plus

  • You've driven a certification or audit cycle end to end yourself.

  • You've automated compliance work, or you're eager to, and you have a view on where AI can help.

  • You've presented risk to senior leaders or a board.

  • You've mentored or onboarded someone before.

🌍 How we work

Location: You must be legally eligible to work from France, Belgium or Spain.

Remote work: We offer remote work flexibility.

 

🎯 Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply, as it can only bring learnings or success.

Remember, this is just a guide, not a checklist. We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

jobs.title: (Senior) Integration Engineer, ERP (Oracle)
jobs.description:
(Senior) Integration Engineer, ERP (Oracle)

Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

BLP only works when it talks to our customers’ ERP systems. As an Integration Engineer, you build and own those connections and keep live integrations running for enterprise customers. Every new ERP system is a new problem to solve. You’ll lead our Oracle integrations across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards, while also contributing to other integrations.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own our integrations with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards and ensure their market fit, usability and reliability.

  • Design and implement interfaces for diverse protocols: REST, SOAP, direct DB access and file transfers.

  • Explore new ERP systems and determine the best way to connect them.

  • Build new ERP integrations, often in close collaboration with pilot customers.

  • Own existing integrations end to end, including issue resolution, and document them so teammates can pick them up.

  • Enable technical project managers to consult on, install and configure mature integrations.

 

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on integration experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, ideally more than one. You have built or maintained interfaces yourself, not only used the system as a functional consultant or key user.

  • Experience with the native interfaces of at least one of these:

    • Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: REST and SOAP web services, File-Based Data Import (FBDI) through the ERP Integration Service, and data extraction with BI Publisher or BI Cloud Connector (BICC).

    • NetSuite: SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL, SuiteScript 2.x (e.g., RESTlets, Map/Reduce scripts), and Token-Based Authentication or OAuth 2.0.

    • JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: AIS Server and Orchestrator, Business Services (BSSV), and Z-file interface tables (e.g., F0411Z1) with their batch processors.

  • A good understanding of purchase-to-pay data in Oracle ERPs: suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and supplier invoice matching.

  • Solid programming skills in at least one backend language. We build our integrations in Go. If you come from Java, C#, Python or similar and are keen to pick up Go, that works for us.

  • A degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • A structured, self-reliant way of working, and ideally experience in a client-facing role.

  • Fluent English. German is a plus, as most of our customers are in the DACH region.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with both cloud (Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite) and on-premise (JD Edwards) environments, and the constraints of each (e.g., no direct database access in Fusion, governance limits in NetSuite).

  • Extensive experience with SQL, common data formats (JSON, XML, CSV) and transports (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP).

  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices: Git, code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD.

  • Integration experience with other ERPs, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Infor.

 

Integration Engineer or Senior Integration Engineer

We hire at both levels. Four things decide where you start: years of experience, breadth of experience, coaching experience and scope.

Integration Engineer

  • Years: 2+ years of hands-on integration work, including Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: in-depth experience with one Oracle ERP and its interfaces.

  • Coaching: you learn quickly from senior colleagues and share what you learn with the team.

  • Scope: you deliver and maintain integrations and resolve issues independently, with guidance on architecture decisions.

Senior Integration Engineer

  • Years: 5+ years of hands-on integration work, several of them with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: integration experience across two or more of Fusion, NetSuite and JD Edwards, or across Oracle and other ERPs, in cloud and on-premise environments.

  • Coaching: you have coached or mentored other engineers and help technical project managers grow.

  • Scope: you own our Oracle integrations end to end, set technical direction and take on the most complex customer cases.

Why BLP

  • Real impact: your integrations decide whether a customer goes live.

  • Breadth: Oracle, Infor, Microsoft Dynamics and many other ERPs, plus EDI and e-invoicing standards.

  • Growth: fast-tracked growth, with promotions and a bonus scheme that includes company shares.

  • Team: regular team events.

Practical information

  • Location: our Zurich office, hybrid with 3+ office days per week, or remotely from anywhere in Europe.

  • If you work remotely, we pay for regular visits and stays in Zurich.

  • Employment: full-time, permanent.

 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

jobs.title: Accounts Payable Associate
jobs.description:
Accounts Payable Associate

LemFi (Series B) is building the go-to financial app for the Global South.


Moving to a new country shouldn’t mean starting from zero. That's why our team of 400+ spanning 20+ countries is building a financial ecosystem that helps immigrants stay connected to home, build stability, and create wealth regardless of where they are from or where they live.


What began as fast, affordable remittances is now evolving into a complete platform for multi-currency accounts, payments, credit, and long-term financial growth.


With millions of users across the globe, we process over $1B in monthly transactions to 30+ countries, proving that borders shouldn't limit financial opportunity.

About the role

LemFi is the financial engine for people the world wasn't built to serve - powering cross-border payments, multi-currency accounts, savings, and credit across 21 countries. Our Finance team sits at the centre of all of it, and the AP function is what keeps the engine running cleanly behind the scenes.


As an Accounts Payable Associate you'll own the end-to-end processing of vendor payments across our UK, US, Canada, Ireland, Norway, Nigeria, and other entities - working across multiple currencies, GL codes, tax jurisdictions, and approval chains. You'll work closely with the wider Finance, Growth, and Operations teams, and you'll have real scope to improve the processes you inherit, not just execute them.

What you'll build and own

  • Process and control vendor invoices across multiple entities and currencies in Tipalti and NetSuite - accurately, on time, every time

  • Perform first-line GL coding, cost-centre allocation, and tax coding (VAT, reverse charge, RCS), flagging anomalies before they become problems

  • Run and support payment cycles - validating bank details, currency, and approval sign-off - and manage the AP inbox with clear, prompt communication to vendors and internal stakeholders

  • Own the monthly AP close: accruals, aged payables review, and reconciliations, with discrepancies surfaced and resolved, not buried

  • Maintain vendor master data (bank details, tax status, W-9/W-8 forms) with tight controls, and support audit requests with clean, well-organised evidence

  • Spot recurring miscoding, duplicate invoices, and process gaps - then help fix them, contributing to automation initiatives (including n8n workflows and NetSuite automation) that reduce manual effort for the whole team

  • Support bank statement uploads and reconciliations for the Reporting team, ensuring transactions post correctly and discrepancies are flagged fast

Your experience

  • 1-3 years in an Accounts Payable, Finance Operations, or transactional finance role

  • Hands-on experience with an AP or ERP system; NetSuite and/or Tipalti strongly preferred

  • Comfortable processing across multiple currencies and entities; exposure to a multi-jurisdiction or group structure is a real advantage

  • Working knowledge of VAT and sales tax concepts - reverse charge, non-deductible VAT, or equivalent

  • Strong Excel skills: lookups, pivot tables, data cleanup, and reconciliation work

  • Detail-oriented and control-conscious, with the ability to prioritise a high volume of transactions and meet payment deadlines without dropping the ball

  • Clear written communicator who can liaise confidently with vendors and internal stakeholders

Nice to have

  • Experience in a fintech, payments, or regulated financial services environment

  • Exposure to automation tools (e.g. n8n) or light scripting for finance workflows

  • Experience supporting external audit requests (KPMG, Crowe, BKL, or similar)


Why Join LemFi?

Love shouldn’t be expensive, yet those working hardest for their families often face predatory fees and banking exclusion. We're changing this.

At LemFi, you won’t be just a cog in a machine. Whether designing products, scaling operations, or telling our story, you’ll tackle complex challenges with real, immediate impact. Your work goes beyond metrics - it puts money back in families’ pockets and offers access to the previously excluded. Join us to make a meaningful difference, where high performance is a lifeline for millions.

You can connect with us on LinkedIn and Instagram and if you haven't already, download the app on the App Store or Google Play.

Recruitment Agencies Notice

LemFi does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruitment agencies. We work only with agencies on our preferred supplier list, and only when we’ve asked them for their support. Any CVs sent to us outside this arrangement will not incur a fee.

LemFi (Series B) is building the go-to financial app for the Global South.

What began as fast, affordable remittances is now evolving into a complete platform for multi-currency accounts, payments, credit, and long-term financial growth.


With millions of users across the globe, we process over $1B in monthly transactions to 30+ countries, proving that borders shouldn't limit financial opportunity.

About the role

LemFi exists to serve people the financial world has largely ignored. Every campaign we run is a chance to reach a diaspora customer who needs a faster, fairer way to send money home, save in multiple currencies, or access credit for the first time. Performance marketing is not a support function here - it is one of the sharpest levers we have for scaling into new corridors and deepening product adoption in the markets we already serve.


As Senior Performance Marketing Manager, you will own paid acquisition end to end across our core channels and geographies. You will set strategy, run the numbers, brief the creatives, and be accountable for CAC, ROAS and volume targets - not just the dashboards that report them. You will work closely with Product, Growth, Creative and Data to make sure every pound, dollar or naira of media spend earns its place. What you'll build and own

  • Own paid media strategy and execution across Meta, Google, TikTok and programmatic, covering customer acquisition and product cross-sell across LemFi's active markets.

  • Manage and optimise significant media budgets with a clear eye on CAC, LTV, ROAS and payback periods - make the numbers work, not just look good in a report.

  • Design and run a rigorous test-and-learn programme across audience segmentation, creative angles, bidding strategies and landing pages, using AI tools to accelerate analysis and iteration.

Love shouldn’t be expensive, yet those working hardest for their families often face predatory fees and banking exclusion. We're changing this.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Lab Automation
jobs.description:
Software Engineer, Lab Automation

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

  • Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

  • Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

  • Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

  • Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

  • Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

  • Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

  • Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

  • Comfortable at the hardware-software boundary. You've built software that drives physical devices, or you're excited to. You can read a protocol spec, debug a flaky connection, and reason about timing.

  • Lab automation experience is a strong plus. Familiarity with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling helps — as does a background in robotics, industrial automation, IoT, or embedded systems.

  • Maker and hacker attitude. You like figuring out how closed systems work and building the thing that makes them work better. Bonus if you're comfortable with electronics, microcontrollers, or a 3D printer when an integration needs a physical fix.

  • AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

  • Self-starter and independent. You define what needs building from how the lab actually works, not just what's in the ticket.

  • Reliability-minded. The lab runs 24/7; you design systems where one instrument failing doesn't cascade through the whole work cell.

Biology background not required — but you should be excited that the code runs real experiments.

Details

  • Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site — you need hands-on access to physical instruments).

  • Type: Full time

  • Start date: ASAP

Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

Behind the API and the AI agents there is a real, physical lab in Lausanne: millions of francs of instruments, freezers full of reagents, deliveries arriving every day, and customer samples going out. When it runs smoothly, a customer gets their results in days. When it does not — a reagent runs out mid-run, a delivery sits unopened, an instrument goes down and nobody noticed the service contract lapsed — experiments stop, and customers feel it immediately.

You are the person who makes sure that does not happen. What is on the shelves, what is on order, what is shipping, and what is about to break — that is yours, and you will run it. This is a hands-on, in-the-lab role, working closely with our Lab Manager and with the scientists whose experiments depend on you getting it right.

This is a good role to be early in your career in. We are going from roughly 25 people to roughly 50 in the next year and multiplying the throughput of the lab, and the person who does this job well will not be doing the same job in two years. We are looking for someone who fixes things rather than reporting them.

What You'll Do

  • Keep the lab stocked. Receive deliveries, unpack them, get them into the right freezer at the right temperature, and make sure our inventory system reflects what is actually on the shelf. Flag what is running low before anyone else notices.

  • Run the day-to-day ordering. Place the orders, chase the ones that are late, and sort out the ones that arrive wrong.

  • Handle shipping, in and out. Customer samples, reagents, equipment. Cold chain, dry ice, customs paperwork, and the courier relationships that make it all land on time.

  • Support the science team hands-on. Reconstituting and aliquoting target proteins, buffer prep, plate handling, and tracking materials in our lab software. You will be at the bench for part of your week.

  • Look after the instruments. Coordinate servicing, calibration, and repairs with vendors, keep the maintenance schedule honest, and get an engineer on site fast when something breaks.

  • Keep the lab safe and organized. Chemical inventory, waste disposal, safety compliance, and the general war against entropy in a shared space.

  • Keep the office and the team running. Supplies, workspace, new-starter setups, and the occasional team event.

  • Help build the new lab. We are expanding into new space. You will be involved in setting it up.

What We're Looking For

  • Some hands-on lab experience. A degree, an apprenticeship, a technician role, or a couple of years in a research or biotech lab. We care much more about whether you are competent and reliable in a lab than about how many years you have logged.

  • Genuinely organized. You are tracking dozens of small things at once — what is on order, what expires next month, which instrument is due for service — and none of them drop.

  • You notice things before they break. The best people in this role are the ones who spot that we are three weeks from running out of a reagent, and quietly fix it, rather than the ones who report the stockout.

  • You are comfortable getting your hands dirty. This is not an administrative job. You will be unpacking boxes, moving dry ice, and reorganizing a freezer that has become someone's junk drawer.

  • You are tech-savvy, and you want to be more so. Our lab runs on our own software and we use AI tooling across the company, including for operational work. We would love someone who ends up automating the boring parts of their own job rather than doing them forever, and we will teach you how. Curiosity here counts for more than existing skill.

  • You want to be in a startup. Priorities move, nothing is fully documented yet, and you will regularly be the first person to do something. If you need a defined process to work inside, this will be uncomfortable.

  • You care about the mission. We are trying to make biology fast and cheap enough that AI can actually do it.

  • Durée : Mission longue durée

  • Type de contrat : Freelance ou CDIC

  • Zone géographique : Occitanie (81)

Contexte de la mission

Dans le cadre d'un programme de construction d'une nouvelle usine industrielle à l'international, prévu sur la période 2028-2032, nous recherchons un profil expérimenté pour intervenir en phase amont d'analyse des besoins et de pré-FEED (Front-End Engineering Design).

La mission consiste à réaliser un audit approfondi de deux usines de production existantes, l'une en France et l'autre en Amérique du Nord, afin d'identifier les bonnes pratiques, les axes d'amélioration et les besoins des différents services.

L'objectif est de recueillir et de formaliser l'ensemble des exigences techniques, fonctionnelles et opérationnelles dans un cahier des charges aussi complet que possible, afin de sécuriser les futures phases d'ingénierie, de conception et de construction de la nouvelle usine.

Missions

  • Réaliser un audit fonctionnel et opérationnel de deux usines de production existantes, situées en France et en Amérique du Nord.

  • Analyser les installations, les méthodes de fonctionnement et les organisations en place afin d'identifier les bonnes pratiques, les points faibles et les axes d'amélioration.

  • Organiser et animer des groupes de travail avec l'ensemble des services concernés, notamment :

    • Maintenance

    • Exploitation et production

    • Process industriels

    • Traitement de l'air

  • Conduire des entretiens et des réunions de travail, notamment à distance via Teams, afin de faire émerger les besoins, contraintes et attentes de chaque service.

  • Challenger les interlocuteurs pour identifier les besoins explicites et implicites, anticiper les problématiques et garantir l'exhaustivité des exigences.

  • Recueillir, analyser et consolider les retours d'expérience des deux sites existants.

  • Identifier les exigences techniques, fonctionnelles, organisationnelles et opérationnelles à intégrer dans la conception de la future usine.

  • Définir les besoins d'industrialisation et les exigences relatives aux process de production.

  • Élaborer et structurer un cahier des charges (CDC) complet et détaillé, intégrant les besoins de l'ensemble des parties prenantes.

  • Rédiger les User Requirement Specifications (URS) afin de formaliser les exigences utilisateurs.

  • Participer à la phase de pré-FEED et contribuer à la définition des orientations techniques du futur site industriel.

  • Assurer la cohérence et l'exhaustivité des exigences afin de limiter les oublis, les modifications tardives et les risques lors des phases ultérieures du projet.

  • Faciliter les échanges entre les différents métiers et accompagner la convergence des besoins vers des spécifications communes.


  • Expérience senior de 10 ans minimum en ingénierie industrielle, conception d'usines de production ou gestion de projets industriels complexes.

  • Expérience significative et confirmée en phase de pré-FEED sur des projets internationaux de construction d'usines de production.

  • Expérience dans des environnements industriels de process, idéalement dans les secteurs de la chimie, de la cosmétique, de l'agroalimentaire ou d'industries de transformation similaires.

  • Solide expérience en audit d'installations industrielles existantes, analyse fonctionnelle et identification des besoins opérationnels.

  • Maîtrise de la rédaction de cahiers des charges techniques et des User Requirement Specifications (URS).

  • Bonne compréhension des enjeux industriels liés aux process, à la maintenance, à l'exploitation, à la production et aux utilités, notamment au traitement de l'air.

  • Capacité à analyser des organisations et installations existantes pour en tirer des recommandations applicables à une construction neuve.

  • Excellentes compétences en animation d'ateliers et en coordination de groupes de travail pluridisciplinaires.

  • Charisme, leadership et forte capacité à faire parler les différents interlocuteurs, y compris sur des besoins non formalisés.

  • Capacité à poser les bonnes questions, challenger les pratiques existantes et faire émerger les attentes de chaque métier.

  • Excellentes capacités d'écoute, d'analyse, de synthèse et de formalisation des exigences.

  • Vision globale des projets industriels et capacité à anticiper les impacts des choix réalisés en phase amont sur les étapes de conception et de construction.

  • Autonomie, rigueur, diplomatie et capacité à fédérer des interlocuteurs aux enjeux parfois divergents.

  • Expérience des environnements multiculturels et des projets industriels internationaux.

  • Anglais professionnel indispensable pour conduire des échanges techniques avec les équipes internationales.

About us

Rentman is a B2B SaaS scale-up building a smart, powerful operations management platform to support event and media production teams. Our users plan everything from small shoots to massive festivals in 70+ countries, and they all rely on Rentman to keep their gear, people, and timing perfectly in sync. Check out our public roadmap to see what’s coming next!

Mission of this role

Getting equipment to and from an event, on time and in one piece, is one of the most critical things our customers do, and one of the hardest. Heavy, specialised, often fragile gear. Fixed vehicle and crew capacity. Round trips rather than one-way drops. Our customers solve this every week, mostly with spreadsheets, phone calls and hard-won instinct.

Transport is a priority on our roadmap, and we're bringing in dedicated ownership to make sure we deliver on it: how customers plan loads, sequence stops and optimise routes across their fleet. This role owns that outcome from the ground up. You'll start by getting close to customers to find the first slice of the problem they'll genuinely want to have solved, ship it, and build the roadmap from there.

Which features ship is yours to decide. You'll be shaping the domain and its roadmap, with the freedom to define how the product takes form. That's a rare amount of ownership for a PM, building something new from first principles, with real trust in how you get there.

What you'll do

  • Own Transport end to end: Running the full release train for your value stream: discovery, scoping, design, development, launch and post-launch tracking.

  • Run customer discovery yourself, in the field: Talk to rental companies about how they plan, staff and execute transport today: warehouse-to-venue routing, multi-stop and multi-vehicle loads, load order, crew and vehicle capacity, and the constraints that make equipment transport harder than generic delivery routing.

  • Define the first sellable increment. Find the smallest thing customers will genuinely pay for, ship it, and be able to explain why that slice was the right first bet.

  • Build and own a sequenced, evidence-based roadmap with the Head of Product, aligned to company goals and product strategy. And explain the prioritisation to sales, support and management so they can plan against it.

  • Translate routing and logistics complexity into buildable scope: multi-stop optimisation, time windows, vehicle and crew capacity, mapping and routing APIs, and the build-vs-buy decisions that come with them.

  • Define success before you build it: Every feature carries a business goal, product briefs stay current, a live dashboard goes up at launch, and you drive go-to-market together with Product Marketing, Support, Sales and Content & Community.

What we are looking for

  • 5+ years as a Product Manager in B2B SaaS.

  • You're comfortable with operationally complex problems: routing, scheduling, fleet or capacity planning, supply chain, field service. A logistics background is a plus, not a must.

  • You work from data. You can show how you set a success metric, what you did when it was missed, and how you make the business case behind a product call.

  • You've run customer discovery yourself, not through a research team, and you can make and defend scope calls on partial evidence.

Nice to haves

  • Product experience in route optimisation, fleet management, field service or supply chain / TMS, or hands-on experience with mapping and routing APIs and platforms (Google Maps Platform, HERE, Mapbox, route-optimisation engines).

PLC Software Engineer - The Netherlands

Ready to build the software behind real-world renewable energy installations?

At Bright Renewables, your PLC software doesn’t stay behind a desk. You’ll see it come to life in complex industrial installations for renewable gas and CO₂ technologies.

As a PLC Software Engineer, you’ll be involved in the complete automation lifecycle - from software design and programming to testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and optimization.

You’ll have the opportunity to contribute to technical decisions, help shape our automation standards, and work alongside experienced colleagues as part of an international software engineering team of around 10 engineers. Together, you’ll collaborate across the Netherlands, Latvia, and Poland to develop and deliver reliable, innovative automation solutions.


Why this role?

You’ll get the opportunity to:

  • Own your solutions - contribute to software solutions throughout the project lifecycle, from design and programming to testing and commissioning;

  • Work on real installations - solve automation challenges in complex renewable energy plants;

  • Have technical influence - contribute to software standards, templates, concepts, and ways of working, within a team that values collaboration and embraces innovative ideas from everyone;

  • Keep developing - work alongside experienced Electrical and Software Engineers and continue building your technical expertise;

  • Work internationally - collaborate with colleagues and project teams in the Netherlands, Poland, Latvia and beyond, including regular international travel to visit our offices and project sites;

  • Choose what works for you - work 32 or 40 hours per week, with flexible starting times and opportunities to work from home;

  • Make an impact - use your automation expertise in technologies that contribute directly to the energy transition.

What will you do?

As a PLC Software Engineer, you design, develop, test, and commission PLC and SCADA control systems for technologies such as gas upgrading and CO₂ liquefaction.

You report directly to the Manager E&I and Software and work closely with Electrical Engineers, Process Engineers and fellow Software Engineers.

Depending on your experience, you’ll also have the opportunity to take more technical ownership, contribute to software concepts and standards, and support colleagues with complex automation challenges.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Designing, programming, testing, and commissioning PLC and SCADA systems;

  • Developing control software for gas upgrading, CO₂ liquefaction, and other renewable energy technologies;

  • Taking ownership of your software from engineering through commissioning;

  • Testing and troubleshooting software during commissioning and operation;

  • Analyzing and resolving software and control-related issues in existing installations;

  • Implementing software updates and optimizations;

  • Supporting Service Engineers with more complex automation and software questions;

  • Contributing to software standards, templates, and automation concepts;

  • Working closely with Electrical Engineers, Software Engineers, and other technical disciplines;

  • Sharing knowledge and supporting colleagues within the engineering team.


What do you bring?

We’re looking for someone who enjoys solving technical challenges and wants to take responsibility for their own engineering work.

Ideally, you have:

  • A completed technical education in automation, mechatronics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field;

  • Several years of experience in PLC/SCADA engineering within an industrial environment;

  • Hands-on experience in PLC programming, ideally with Siemens S7 and TIA Portal, combined with knowledge of WinCC SCADA, industrial communication networks, and remote access solutions.

  • Experience with commissioning and troubleshooting industrial installations;

  • A good understanding of automation architectures and industrial control systems;

  • Good command of English, both spoken and written;

  • Knowledge of OT security is a plus.

What’s in it for you?

We want to give you the technical freedom and working environment to do your best engineering work.

You can expect:

  • A competitive salary based on your experience and technical background;

  • The option to work 32 or 40 hours per week;

  • Flexible starting times between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m. ;

  • Ample opportunities to work from home, including a one-time €250 allowance to set up your home office;

  • An attractive annual profit-sharing scheme for employees with at least 12 months of service;

  • An excellent pension scheme;

  • 8% annual holiday allowance;

  • A commuting allowance of €0.23 per kilometer, in accordance with our employment conditions;

  • A high level of autonomy and responsibility;

  • Plenty of opportunities for technical and professional development;

  • An international engineering environment with both experienced professionals and engineers earlier in their careers;

  • The opportunity to work with renewable energy technologies and contribute directly to the energy transition;

  • A bike lease program and rewards for cycling to work;

  • A modern, sustainably built working environment in Hengelo.

About Bright Renewables

Bright Renewables develops and delivers technologies for renewable gas and CO₂ capture, providing solutions from engineering and realization through to service and maintenance. Our installations convert biogas into renewable natural gas and capture, purify, and liquefy CO₂ for industrial reuse.

We are part of HoSt Group, a family-owned Dutch company operating internationally in renewable energy technology.

For you, that means working on international projects with the opportunities of a global organization, while keeping the short communication lines, technical freedom, and personal approach of a family-owned company.

jobs.description:
Staff Software Engineer

This role is part of our Prerender team, one of our growing brands at saas.group.

For nearly a decade, Prerender has empowered marketers to create dynamic, complex sites at scale, making their JavaScript websites easily indexable by search engines. We eliminate indexing and crawling limitations, allowing our customers to gain the upper-hand on HTML sites and rank higher on SERPs. More than 100,000 websites around the globe trust Prerender to serve more than 2.7 billion web pages to crawlers to improve organic search ranking.

Profile Overview

As a Staff Engineer at Prerender, you amplify effectiveness across teams, systems, and practices. You’re deeply hands-on, but your biggest impact comes from enabling others to move faster, safer, and with greater confidence. You lead major architectural evolutions, coach engineers in XP principles, and help teams make sound technical decisions that scale across the organization.

This role combines strategic thinking with practical execution; you’ll shape the technical direction of our distributed rendering platform, align teams on shared goals, and create the conditions for consistent, high-quality delivery.

If you’re motivated by simplifying complexity, raising the bar for technical excellence, and empowering others to do their best work, you’ll thrive here.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead by doing: Contribute to core systems while modeling high standards in code quality, testing, and design.
  • Guide architectural evolution: Drive cross-team initiatives that move our systems toward simplicity, scalability, and testability.
  • Coach and mentor: Support engineers at all levels through pairing, design reviews, and hands-on coaching in XP practices.
  • Simplify complexity: Design elegant solutions to deep technical challenges in performance, reliability, and distributed rendering.
  • Unblock and empower: Spot risks early, resolve systemic bottlenecks, and establish good defaults that let teams move quickly and confidently.
  • Champion sustainable quality: Promote practices like TDD, pair programming, and continuous delivery to keep development fast without sacrificing stability.
  • Align strategy and execution: Partner with product and leadership to balance short-term delivery with long-term technical health.

How We Work

At Prerender, Staff Engineers influence through context, coaching, and example. You don’t gatekeep, you unblock, empower, and guide.

  • Influence through impact: You lead architectural direction and help teams make sound trade-offs that scale across systems and squads.
  • Think in systems: You see the connections between teams, technologies, and workflows, and help align them toward cohesive solutions.
  • Build shared context: You create clarity across teams, helping others understand not just what we’re building, but why.
  • Improve the ecosystem: You refine tooling, automation, and engineering practices that raise effectiveness across the organization.
  • Model balance: You help the org sustain both fast delivery and long-term maintainability.

A Typical Day Might Involve

  • Pairing with a team to untangle a tricky performance issue or refactor a shared library
  • Leading a design discussion that impacts multiple services or teams
  • Coaching an engineer through an architectural decision or trade-off
  • Collaborating with product and leadership to align technical investments with business goals
  • Reviewing code and providing thoughtful, actionable feedback
  • Improving CI/CD pipelines or internal tooling to make development smoother and safer
  • Helping define patterns, guardrails, or “good defaults” that raise consistency across teams

What We’re Looking For

  • Proven experience: 10+ years designing and shipping complex, distributed systems
  • Architectural leadership: A track record of leading large-scale technical initiatives that simplified and strengthened core systems
  • Deep technical skill: Expertise in modern backend development - ideally in TypeScript/Node.js or Golang, plus familiarity with AWS and cloud-native infrastructure
  • Systems thinking: The ability to see across layers of the stack, connecting product goals with technical architecture
  • Coaching mindset: You elevate others through context, guidance, and example
  • Strategic clarity: You balance short-term priorities with long-term sustainability and technical health
  • Strong communicator: You make complex ideas clear to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Bias for improvement: You’re always looking for ways to make systems, teams, and practices better

Bonus if you’ve worked in SEO, web performance, or large-scale rendering infrastructure, but curiosity and adaptability matter more than specific domain expertise.

What’s in it for You

  • Ultimate flexibility: We’re 100% remote. You can work from wherever you like, whenever you like.
  • Freedom and autonomy: We’re a high-trust team, and you’ll be given lots of flexibility to solve problems in your own way — with plenty of help from the team when you need it.
  • Minimum bureaucracy: We don’t like to get bogged down with meetings and red tape. We like to be efficient and keep momentum steady & sustainable.
  • Small & friendly team: We help each other out, have fun, and joke around.
  • Our network: We are a community of entrepreneurial SaaS professionals that regularly exchange ideas, knowledge, learning and expertise with each other internally.
  • Flexible time off: We want you to recharge your batteries when needed.

Prerender is part of saas.group and we have a shared goal of succeeding together.

What is saas.group?

Think of us as the driving catalyst behind your favorite software success stories. saas.group, established in 2017, is on a mission to turbocharge promising B2B SaaS ventures, unlocking their full potential. As a Software-as-a-Service portfolio powerhouse, we specialize in acquiring small software treasures and polishing them into industry stars. With a dynamic, fully remote team of nearly 380+ colleagues spanning 50+ countries we are truly global and we are rewriting the playbook on SaaS innovation and collaboration. We grow 23 exciting brands under our umbrella. Feel free to explore our Candidate's Hub to get an insider's view, dive into our culture, gain valuable insights into our teams and how we work.

Also, don’t forget to follow saas.group on LinkedIn to stay up-to-date on our job openings, podcast episodes, and with all things happening at our company.

We don’t just simply offer you to “take a job with us” but rather to “join us on this journey” to build the world's largest platform of independent SaaS companies.

Sounds like something you’re up for? Feel free to apply even if you don’t check all these boxes. We believe in the power of diversity and fresh perspectives to spice up our team. Your application might just be the missing ingredient!

jobs.description:
People Operations Partner

📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

🚀 The Role

We're hiring a People Operations Partner to join our Performance team.

tem is rebuilding the energy transaction - transparent, fair and built on trust. Behind that mission is a company growing fast, and a Performance team that's already lean and stretched. Core People operations needs more firepower as we scale, and there's a direct commercial angle too: a strong People Operations function is what lets new joiners ramp up and become productive faster once they arrive.

This is a multi-disciplinary People Operations role at the centre of the employee lifecycle - equal parts operational delivery, automation and continuous improvement. You'll be the reliable hands keeping People processes running as we scale, from multi-country payroll to onboarding, employee changes and offboarding. You'll also build the tools, automations and lightweight AI workflows that connect our systems (Rippling, Notion, Linear, Slack, Ashby, n8n and Google Workspace), so the function doesn't need to double in size every time headcount does.

In your first 12 months, you might:

  • Take ownership of payroll across our UK and employer-of-record employees, keeping every cycle accurate and on time as pay schedules and countries multiply.

  • Become the trusted point of contact for employees and managers, owning their queries through to resolution.

  • Build the automations and AI-enabled workflows that remove repetitive manual work from the employee lifecycle.

  • Turn recurring pain points into better processes, tools or self-service, and measure whether they actually worked.

  • Move across People disciplines as priorities shift - reward and benchmarking, pensions and options administration, performance cycles, engagement and people data.

🛠️ Responsibilities

  • Run payroll end to end: own monthly payroll across UK and employer-of-record employees - changes, corrections, off-cycle and ex-gratia payments, contractor payroll and invoicing, and country-specific items - keeping it accurate and on time as we add pay schedules and countries.

  • Keep the lifecycle running: deliver core People operations across onboarding, employee changes, contracts and documentation, leave, mobility (visas and international moves), EOR and contractor setup, and offboarding, flexing into whatever the business needs most.

  • Be the trusted point of contact: own employee and manager queries through to resolution with a clear response standard, rather than passing them between functions.

  • Keep the foundations accurate: maintain employee data, documentation and systems so that everything else can depend on them.

  • Automate the repeatable: build and maintain automations and lightweight AI-enabled tools, workflows and agents that connect Rippling, Notion, Linear, Slack, Ashby, n8n, Google Workspace and similar, and remove repetitive manual work - with controls so speed never costs accuracy, privacy or employee trust.

  • Own the People tech stack: evolve our People technology ecosystem - evaluate emerging tools, consolidate where we can, and simplify the architecture.

  • Improve continuously: turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service, measure whether they worked, and give foundational People processes a named owner and a runbook someone else could follow cold.

  • Design to delight and to scale: we treat our people like top athletes and aim to delight at every step of the employee journey, and what works at today's size shouldn't need twice the People team when headcount doubles - default to eliminating or automating work rather than administering it.

  • Partner across the business: work with Finance, Legal, Talent, Performance Partners and functional specialists to turn People initiatives into scalable services, and build dashboards and lightweight analysis that help the team and the business make better decisions.

✅ Requirements

Must-Haves

  • You've worked in People Operations, People Services, HR Operations or another operational People role - generalists welcome - and you hold a high bar on accuracy and confidentiality.

  • You've run payroll cycles end to end, ideally multi-country, in-house or through an employer of record. UK fundamentals (PAYE, RTI, pension auto-enrolment, statutory payments) are familiar, or clearly learnable fast if your payroll experience comes from another market.

  • You're highly comfortable with technology: AI is part of how you work, you actively experiment with new tools and capabilities, and you can build automations through no-code or low-code tools, integrations and AI workflows.

  • You think in systems and workflows rather than individual tasks, with a strong instinct for simplification ("why are we doing this manually?"), and you're comfortable using data to diagnose problems and make decisions.

  • You operate effectively in ambiguity, without waiting for a perfectly defined process or remit, and you balance efficiency with empathy - People Operations is about people, not just workflows.

  • Strong ownership instincts: when something's broken, unclear or inefficient, your instinct is to fix it, and you're willing to move across People disciplines depending on where the organisation needs you.

Desirable

  • Breadth across the People remit beyond Operations - reward and benchmarking, pensions, benefits, or performance and engagement. This role is deliberately multi-disciplinary.

  • Familiarity with the basics of UK and EU employment law, and experience administering equity or share options (for example EMI or unapproved schemes, and cap-table tools such as Vestd).

  • Experience supporting international employment through employers of record, and setting up or managing contractors (including off-payroll and IR35 awareness).

  • Experience in a fast-scaling startup or scale-up, especially through a period of doubling headcount or entering new countries.

🎁 Benefits & Perks

  • Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission.

  • 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

  • Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,400 per year for your remote setup.

  • Up to GBP150 or EUR170 per month for wellbeing.

🤝 Interview Process

We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know.

  • Intro call with our Talent team.

  • Hiring Manager interview.

  • Skills interview, which might include a practical exercise.

  • Bar Raiser interview with leadership stakeholders.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

Bid Manager UK (all genders)

Your Mission

About the Role
We are looking for a proactive and commercially minded Bid Manager to lead and project manage the end-to-end tender and proposal process across our UK business.
You will take ownership of each bid from early qualification and planning through to submission, clarification, handover and post-bid review. This includes setting the bid strategy, defining responsibilities, coordinating contributors, managing timelines and dependencies, and ensuring that decisions and deliverables are completed to the required quality and deadline.
The role requires someone who can bring structure and momentum to complex tender processes, engage stakeholders across different functions and levels, and constructively challenge assumptions, contributions and proposed solutions. Working closely with Commercial, Operations, Delivery, Product, Legal, Finance and central teams, you will ensure that submissions are compliant, compelling, deliverable and commercially robust.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own and manage the full bid lifecycle from opportunity qualification and bid planning through to submission, clarification, contract handover and post-bid review.
  • Develop and maintain clear bid plans covering deliverables, responsibilities, dependencies, review stages, approvals, resources and deadlines.
  • Lead bid kick-offs, progress reviews, solution workshops and final submission reviews, creating clarity and accountability across all contributors.
  • Coordinate and actively manage internal stakeholders, external consultants and specialist partners, challenging delays, unclear ownership or insufficient contributions.
  • Identify bid risks, dependencies, gaps and decision requirements early, escalating where necessary to protect quality, commercial viability and timelines.
  • Lead bid qualification and go/no-go assessments, ensuring that client requirements and commercial, technical, operational and delivery implications are fully understood.
  • Develop the bid strategy, win themes, key messages and overall proposal structure in collaboration with relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure that submissions are compliant, persuasive, commercially competitive and operationally deliverable, constructively challenging assumptions and proposed commitments.
  • Own the overall quality and consistency of proposal content, turning cross-functional input into one clear, client-focused response.
  • Maintain an accurate tender pipeline and clear reporting on opportunity status, key dates, resource requirements, risks and decisions.
  • Improve bid-management tools, governance and reusable content, including Jira-based planning and appropriate use of AI-supported bidding solutions.
  • Ensure a structured handover of successful bids, including commitments, assumptions, risks, dependencies, SLAs and implementation obligations, to Delivery and Operations.

Your profile

What We're Looking For

  • Proven experience leading complex bids, proposals or tender processes from qualification through to submission and handover.
  • Strong project-management skills, including planning, stakeholder coordination, risk management, governance and action tracking.
  • Confidence coordinating and constructively challenging contributors across different functions and levels of seniority.
  • Ability to create accountability and maintain momentum without relying on formal authority.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex input into clear and persuasive proposals.
  • Strong commercial judgement and the ability to understand client priorities, operational constraints and business risks.
  • Ability to identify gaps, dependencies and unrealistic commitments early and drive timely decisions.
  • Highly organised and comfortable managing several concurrent deadlines and changing priorities.
  • Experience with public-sector procurement, framework agreements or infrastructure tenders would be highly advantageous.
  • Experience in EV charging, energy, transport, mobility, utilities or related infrastructure, and familiarity with Jira, CRM or proposal-management tools, would be beneficial.

Our Offer

Location & Ways of Working

Location
ubitricity Distributed Energy Systems UK Ltd.
Spectrum House, Unit 11
32-34 Gordon House Road
London NW5 1LP

We operate a hybrid working model and believe that collaboration is at its best when people spend time together. Employees are expected to work from the office a minimum of three days per week, including our dedicated Face-to-Face Tuesday, which is designed to strengthen cross-team collaboration, knowledge sharing, and innovation.

Benefits
At ubitricity, we offer a competitive benefits package designed to support your health, wellbeing, financial security, and professional growth.

Time Off & Flexibility

Health & Wellbeing

  • Company-funded Benefit-in-Kind (BIK) tax and National Insurance contributions related to the healthcare benefit
  • Option to add family members to the healthcare scheme (employee-funded)
  • Access to the Spark Health & Wellbeing Platform, including:

    • Online physiotherapy
    • Confidential counselling support

Financial Benefits

  • Additional employer pension contribution of:
    • £50 per month for employees enrolled in private healthcare
    • £100 per month for employees who opt out of private healthcare
  • Automatic enrolment into the NEST pension scheme (subject to eligibility)

Additional Benefits

Why Join Us?
At ubitricity, we're helping accelerate the transition to electric mobility by delivering innovative EV charging solutions across the UK and Europe. As part of the Shell Group, we combine the agility of a growing technology business with the scale and opportunities of a global organisation.
You'll join a collaborative, international team where your ideas are valued, your development is supported, and your work has a direct impact on the future of sustainable transport. Health can’t wait.

Alan exists to end the wait.

It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

⭐️ The Account Executive (mid-market) job

We’re expanding our Sales team in France and are looking for ‘full-stack’ Sales to engage with prospects and turn them into happy Alan customers. You will join a team that focuses on companies from one of the following segments: Tech & Engineering, Business Services & Media, Retail, Transport, HCR, Learn & Care, Food & Beverage or Metallurgy.

You will interact with everyone from HR executives to CEOs.

Meet Hakim in this article to learn more about makes the Metallurgy segment so interesting for an Account Executive.

  • Growth opportunity: The addressable market is enormous, offering virtually unlimited opportunities for growth.

What will you do with us?

You’ll own the entire sales cycle, from prospecting to closing. The average sales cycle is 4-6 months, dealing with companies ranging from 30 to 300 employees, with an average ARR of 150K€.

At Alan, Account Executives drive deals and close strategic opportunities with prospects. We sometimes handle some customer relationships to ensure the best possible onboarding. You’ll educate prospects, provide inspiring product demos, and onboard key stakeholders, making the transition from prospect to customer seamless.

Meet Fanny Cibot who is Account Executive within the Business Services & Media Crew.

  • Are eager to learn fast and make an impact from day 1;

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range.

If you're still wondering whether this could be the best move for you, take a look at this article from Lucie Leflour, our Sales Lead in France.


Everything else is a plus. We care about having a diversity of experiences, profiles and backgrounds in our team.


🙌   Perks & Benefits

Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture.

R&D Mechanical Engineer

As a R&D Mechanical Engineer within our Mechanical team, you will lead development of mechanical systems and subsystems of our next-generation surgical robot from the early concept to the to a verified product.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

R&D & Mechatronic Subsystem Design

• Lead the end-to-end design and development of high-precision mechatronic subsystems for surgical robotics, translating clinical and industrial design inputs into simple and robust mechanical solutions.

• Execute detailed design work utilizing 3D CAD (Solidworks), finite element analysis (FEA), and worst-case tolerance stack-up analyses. And applying DFM/DFA principles to optimize cost, yield, and assembly efficiency.

• Collaborate within cross-functional R&D teams (Electrical, Software, Systems, and Clinical) to rapidly prototype, validate, and iterate robotic platforms and subsystems.

Verification, Testing & Tooling

• Architect, build and document custom mechatronic test benches and automated test fixtures for design verification, fatigue testing, and end-of-line production testing.

• Author and execute verification protocols and reports to prove subsystem performance against medical device requirements.

Design Transfer & Supply Chain

• Support Design Transfer to Contract Manufacturers, by transferring technical knowledge to industrialization teams, reviewing Work Instructions and pFMEAs, and supporting process-specific tool development.

• Support mechanical supplier selection and qualification, support root-cause analyses for supplier-related quality issues (NC/CAPA).

Medical Device Compliance & Lifecycle

• Maintain full compliance with medical device standards (e.g., ISO 13485, IEC 60601-1, ISO 14971) and author compliant Design History File (DHF) documentation.

• Plan and execute Engineering Change Requests, ensuring robust risk management and traceability.

• Chair formal technical design reviews and present architectural decisions to cross-departmental stakeholders and leadership.

Requirements

Work Experience and Education requirements:

• Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics or a related engineering discipline.

• Relevant Experience: Minimum of 3+ years of professional mechanical design experience, with ideally direct expertise in collaborative robots (cobots), robotics platforms, or high-precision robotic joints/actuators.

• Full-Lifecycle DFX Mastery: Proven track record in end-to-end product design, incorporating Design for Excellence principles:

o Design for Manufacturability & Assembly (DFM/DFA)

o Design to Cost (DTC)
