Data Full Stack

Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

⭐️ The Data Team

  • Being part of Alan's data team means you'll have a positive impact on people's health and wellbeing.

  • We create insights to help our colleagues focus on what is most impactful.

  • We build features and tools powered by data that directly help our members.

    • going deep into health consumption patterns,

    • understanding our product usage,

    • creating visibility to help our sales team perform,

    • automating how we reimburse our members,

We also believe in having a full stack approach:

  • Each one of us contributes to all 3 aspects of the data spectrum (analytics, engineering, science). This encourages strong ownership and drives impact.

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
Strategic Partnerships Lead

About DataSnipper

Audit is the bedrock of the global economy. DataSnipper builds the AI that auditors and finance teams rely on to do that work with confidence: agents designed around how audits are actually performed, a platform firms trust with their most sensitive client evidence, and a team built around former auditors who know the work firsthand. We want to define how the profession works in the age of AI.

More than 600,000 professionals across 175 countries use DataSnipper, including all Big Four firms, Fortune 500 companies, and government agencies. In 2025 alone, we delivered over $1.4 billion in productivity savings for our customers. Backed by Index Ventures and Insight Partners, we are one of the fastest-growing companies in AI for audit, and the fastest-growing tech company in the Netherlands two years running.

Everything we build starts from one principle: AI in audit has to be something professionals can trust, verify, and defend. Joining now means helping lead the profession's shift from manual testing to agentic execution.


The Role


Partnerships are one of DataSnipper's most important growth levers. Across every major market, the consulting firms, technology platforms, and professional networks that organizations rely on shape which technologies their teams and clients adopt. As AI changes how audit work gets done, those partners are deciding who to build with.

As Strategic Partnerships Lead, you will lead, build, and launch DataSnipper's partnerships across Europe and the wider EMEA region, spanning our consulting alliances, key technology partners, and strategic relationships across the audit ecosystem and beyond. Our European ecosystem already includes relationships with leading consulting firms and regional networks. Your job is to scale it, and to build what comes next: new partner programs, new markets, and new commercial models.

This is an entrepreneurial, quota-carrying role with a broad remit and room to build. You will report to the Global Partnerships Leader and work closely with our EMEA Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Marketing teams.


What You Will Work On

  • Own and grow a portfolio of strategic partners across Europe, including consulting firms, technology platforms, and regional networks, and act as their senior counterpart at DataSnipper.

  • Scale existing partnerships into multi-country programs, and launch new ones market by market, adapting to local regulatory, commercial, and cultural nuances.

  • Source, assess, and close new partnerships, from referral and co-sell arrangements to resell models, prioritized against DataSnipper's growth goals.

  • Work with consulting partners to help them advise their clients on bringing AI into audit and finance, with DataSnipper at the center of that work.

  • Build joint go-to-market plans with each partner, covering account mapping, co-selling, events, and executive engagement, that turn relationships into pipeline and closed revenue.

  • Deepen key technology partnerships across the region to unlock co-sell, marketplace, and joint solution opportunities.

  • Create the enablement, playbooks, and co-marketing assets partners need to position and deliver DataSnipper with confidence.

  • Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue targets, and report on performance with clear, honest data.

  • Bring partner feedback from across Europe back into DataSnipper, so what you hear in the field shapes product, packaging, and pricing.

  • Be a visible face of DataSnipper across the region, at partner summits, field events, and industry forums.

  • Willingness to embrace global business and travel.

What You Bring

  • 5 to 7 years of experience in partnerships, business development, or a senior commercial role, ideally in B2B SaaS, AI, or financial technology.

  • A proven track record of independently managing and growing complex, multi-stakeholder partnerships from identification through to revenue impact.

  • Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to negotiate partnership structures, co-sell agreements, and commercial terms with senior counterparts.

  • Experience building joint go-to-market programs and driving pipeline through partner channels across more than one European market.

  • Excellent relationship-building and influencing skills, with the credibility to work as a peer with firm leadership, from alliance leads to managing directors and partners.

  • Existing relationships with consulting firm leadership in Europe are a strong advantage.

How You Work

  • Entrepreneurial. When you spot a gap, you build what fills it, playbook or not.

  • High standards. You hold yourself, and the partners you work with, to a high bar.

  • Close to the work. You dig into how audit gets done, how firms make decisions, and where AI changes the economics.

  • Accountable. You measure yourself by results, and you own them when they fall short.

  • Fast and rigorous. You move quickly without cutting corners, because in audit the details matter.

  • Generous with your team. You share what you learn, give credit freely, and make the people and partners around you better.

Why This Role, Why Now

  • Momentum: Used across the world's leading audit institutions, including all Big Four firms. A $100M Series B led by Index Ventures at a $1B valuation, building on earlier investment from Insight Partners. Ranked #1 on the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 in 2023 and 2024, named to the Forbes Fintech 50 for 2026, and one of the fastest-growing companies in AI for audit.

  • Extraordinary team: Former Big Four auditors and audit leaders, AI engineers and researchers, and operators who have scaled category-defining software companies. Headquartered in Amsterdam, with teams across New York, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. You will be surrounded by people who are exceptional at what they do and generous with what they know.

  • Scope: You will shape how one of DataSnipper's most important growth channels scales, with direct visibility to leadership.

  • Impact: The partnerships you build will influence how the world's leading firms adopt AI across audit and assurance.

What we offer

 

  • Being part of one of the fastest-growing scale-ups in the Netherlands

  • Make an impact by disrupting the audit industry with us

  • 28 vacation days

  • Excellent salary

  • Pension plan

  • Stock participation plan

  • Hybrid work (Amsterdam-based)

  • International team and environment

  • Daily lunch 🍽️

  • Mental health support (OpenUp)

  • Social events and team activities 🤩

At DataSnipper, we believe great ideas come from different perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds. We’re committed to building an inclusive workplace and providing a fair and equitable hiring experience for every candidate.

We welcome applicants regardless of age, race, ethnicity, nationality, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or any other characteristic that makes you, you.

jobs.title: System Architect
jobs.description:
System Architect

Are you an experienced System Architect with a passion for intelligent building management systems, industrial automation, and safety-critical applications? At Deerns, you will have the opportunity to work on innovative and challenging projects that contribute to a smarter, safer, and more sustainable future. Read on and discover how you can make an impact.

The challenge 

The System Architect for Intelligent Building Management Solutions and Industrial Automation plays a crucial role in designing integrated automation solutions for both buildings and industrial processes. This position involves developing safe, efficient, and future-ready systems that connect various installations, such as HVAC, lighting, access control, gas safety, and industrial process control. You will work closely with project teams, suppliers, and end-users to create innovative and sustainable solutions that meet the highest safety standards.

Your responsibilities include: 

  • Developing automation architectures: Design scalable solutions for intelligent building management and process automation, including gas detection systems, safety mechanisms, and process control.

  • System integration: Connect installations using protocols like BACnet, Modbus, KNX, and industrial standards such as OPC UA and PROFIBUS.

  • Gas safety and process safety: Develop solutions for gas detection, emergency shutdowns, ventilation integration, and fail-safe control systems for industrial environments.

  • Specification and standards management: Implement relevant standards for intelligent building management solutions, process automation, and safety systems, such as IEC 61511 (functional safety) and ATEX regulations.

  • Process optimization: Analyze and optimize industrial processes and systems to enhance efficiency, safety, and sustainability.

  • Stakeholder management: Collaborate effectively with various stakeholders, including clients, end-users, engineers, and project managers, ensuring solutions meet both functional and technical requirements.

  • Continuous learning and development: Stay updated on the latest innovations in smart technologies and automation, applying these to develop improved, future-proof solutions. • Technological consulting: Identify innovations to enhance performance and reliability in intelligent buildings and industrial environments.

  • Documentation and communication: Prepare technical documentation and communicate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders.

Required Skills and Competencies:

  • Extensive knowledge of intelligent building management solutions, gas safety systems, and industrial process control.

  • Expertise in communication standards and protocols such as KNX, BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA, and PROFIBUS.

  • Proficiency in designing fail-safe systems and safety-critical applications.

  • Experience with IT networks and cybersecurity in automation environments.

  • Strong analytical skills and problem-solving abilities.

  • Flexibility and the ability to continuously adapt to technological advancements.

  • Excellent communication skills to clearly present complex technical issues

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Automation Technology, or a related field.

  • Relevant experience in intelligent building management solutions, industrial automation, and safety-critical systems. This role combines technological innovation with safety-critical applications. As a System Architect, you will develop integrated solutions that maximize comfort, safety, efficiency, and sustainability in both buildings and industrial processes.

We offer 

  • A position of 32-40 hours per week with a salary to match. 

  • Challenging projects for leading clients in the Netherlands and internationally. 

  • A work environment in which innovation and sustainability are put into practice daily. 

  • Attention to your own development and vitality with ample training and development opportunities, bicycle and sports arrangements, flexible working hours, 33 vacation days and the possibility of purchasing additional days. 

  • Hybrid working, where you have the opportunity to alternate between working from home and the office. 

  • A team where cooperation and collegiality are priority, and where we interact informally. 

  • Sustainability is in our genes. This is expressed, for example, in a mobility policy where health and sustainability are most important. Many of our offices are located near public transport hubs, cycling is encouraged, and your travel expenses are reimbursed 100% on the basis of public transport. 

 

About Deerns 
As an independent engineering firm, Deerns specializes in consultancy, design and implementation supervision in the fields of installation engineering, building physics, energy supply and sustainability. Our areas of expertise contribute to sustainable, intelligent and future-proof buildings that optimally support our clients' processes. We are responsible for designing the installations and realizing good comfort and a pleasant climate in a wide variety of buildings; from offices, to airports and from hospitals to data centers. 
 

In addition, Deerns has been named a World Class Workplace for 2026! 

 

Want to know more? 
Would you like to know more about working at Deerns? Then contact Maarten Borgmeijer (Corporate Recruiter) at +31 6 11 66 75 44. Would you like to know more about the role itself? Then please contact Ester Vlielander (Unit Director Electronics / Data Centers / Life Sciences) at +31 6 50 73 68 41

Apollo has hundreds of technical integrations across its ecosystem. Only a select few graduate into full Technology Alliances — partnerships significant enough to warrant real commercial investment: co-selling, joint go-to-market programs, and coordinated effort across product, marketing, sales, and partnerships. This is where Apollo puts the large majority of its focus and resources once an integration has proven it's worth building a genuine alliance around.

You'll own 360-degree responsibility for a select group of Apollo's most important technology alliances — the commercial and relationship layer that turns a technical integration into a real go-to-market motion. Where Product Partnerships owns integration depth and breadth (the technical relationship with each partner's R&D org), you own everything commercial: field-level co-selling, joint business planning, co-marketing execution, and stakeholder alignment from the executive level down to the field. You'll start by owning and running a focused portfolio of these alliances yourself. As Apollo's technology alliance ecosystem and revenue contribution scale, you'll hire and lead a team of Technology Partner Managers to carry that portfolio forward.

What you'll do:

1. Own 360-Degree Alliance Relationships

  • Take full ownership — commercial, relational, and operational — of a select portfolio of Apollo's graduated technology alliances
  • Build and maintain joint business plans with each partner, and be the single point of accountability for the health and growth of the relationship
  • Work with Product Partnerships to help decide which integrations are ready to graduate into a full alliance, and which alliances need to evolve or wind down

2. Drive Field-Level Co-Selling and Revenue

  • Get Apollo's own sales org and each partner's sales org actually selling together, not just aware of each other
  • Broker rep-to-rep introductions and build the field enablement that makes co-selling easy on both sides
  • Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue as a core, measurable outcome of the role

3. Design and Run Co-Marketing Programs

  • Build joint go-to-market programs that span demand generation, field events, and content — not one-off co-marketing moments
  • Partner with Apollo's marketing team to execute programs that generate real pipeline, not just brand association

4. Align Stakeholders Across the Business

  • Drive alignment across every level of the organization — from executive sponsors to management to the field — on each alliance's priorities and goals
  • Be the connective tissue between Partnerships, Product, Marketing, and Sales for each alliance you own

5. Build and Lead the Team as You Scale

  • Start as an individual contributor, personally owning and running a focused portfolio of alliances
  • As the technology alliance ecosystem and revenue contribution grow, hire, coach, and lead a team of Technology Partner Managers
  • Design how ownership divides as the team grows — by partner, partner type, or motion — and build the operating rhythm (QBRs, planning cadence, reporting) the team runs on

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years in technology alliances, strategic partnerships, or channel roles, with a demonstrated track record driving partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue

  • A track record designing and running joint go-to-market programs across demand generation, field events, and content, in partnership with a marketing team
  • Proven ability to align stakeholders across levels (executive, management, field) and across functions (product, marketing, sales, partnerships) around a shared plan
  • Comfortable starting as an individual contributor owning a personal portfolio, with a clear trajectory toward hiring and leading a team as the function scales

Preferred Qualifications

Manager, Machine Learning Engineering

About Tala

Tala is the AI-native credit infrastructure that connects global capital to the global majority. We combine proprietary risk intelligence with an expanding network of capital and distribution partners to power credit access at scale. To date, Tala has distributed more than $9 billion in capital to more than 14 million customers across Africa, Latin America, and Asia, building the definitive contextual dataset on thin-file borrowers in emerging markets. Tala is now converting that foundation into shared infrastructure that partners, capital providers, and ecosystems can build on.

The company has been named to the Fortune Impact 20 list, CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies twice, CNBC Disruptor 50 for five years, and Forbes’ Fintech 50 list for ten years running.

Given the global nature of our team, we operate on a remote-first approach with office hubs in Santa Monica, CA (HQ); Nairobi, Kenya; Mexico City, Mexico; Manila, the Philippines; and Bangalore, India.

Most Talazens join us because they connect with our mission. If you are energized by the impact you can make at Tala, we’d love to hear from you!

The Role

We’re looking for a Manager, Machine Learning Engineering to lead Tala’s ML Platform team. This person will manage a team of Machine Learning Engineers responsible for building the platforms, frameworks, and infrastructure that enable our Data Science teams to securely train, deploy, monitor, and operate machine learning models at scale.

This is a player-coach management role. You’ll be responsible for developing and growing the team while also providing enough technical leadership to guide architecture, engineering practices, reliability, and production systems. The role has a particular focus on real-time machine learning inference and streaming data systems, as well as the platforms that support batch model development and deployment.

What You'll Do

Lead & Grow the Team

  • Manage and develop a team of 4–6 Machine Learning Engineers across mid-to-senior levels.
  • Hire, source, interview, and close strong MLE talent.
  • Establish clear expectations, provide regular feedback, and create development plans for direct reports.
  • Coach engineers toward growth and promotion while addressing performance gaps directly and thoughtfully.
  • Create opportunities for engineers to take on challenging projects and grow their technical leadership.

Own Engineering Delivery

  • Set quarterly goals and ensure the team consistently delivers against them.
  • Own prioritization across product roadmap work, run-the-business activities, and operational excellence.
  • Balance team capacity across new development, maintenance, technical debt, and production support.
  • Improve team productivity by reducing context switching and delegating effectively.
  • Partner with engineers and technical leads to estimate and scope complex work.

Provide Technical Leadership

  • Guide the development of platforms and frameworks that allow Data Scientists and Analysts to explore data, develop features, and train, test, deploy, and monitor ML models.
  • Provide technical leadership across model infrastructure, real-time inference, streaming feature extraction, batch processing, and production ML systems.
  • Drive strong engineering practices around testing, automation, observability, fault tolerance, infrastructure-as-code, and deployment.
  • Own and improve SLOs, on-call health, capacity planning, reliability, and incident response.
  • Review technical designs and help drive architectural standards and technical debt reduction.

Partner Across the Organization

  • Work closely with Data Science, Data Engineering, Data Platform, Product, Credit, and Business Development teams.
  • Translate business and technical needs into scalable ML platform solutions.
  • Coordinate dependencies and delivery across multiple engineering and data teams.
  • Help create structure and clarity in an environment where priorities and requirements can evolve.

What You'll Need

Management Experience

  • 2+ years of directly managing engineers, including hiring, performance management, coaching, and career development.
  • Experience managing a team through at least one full performance cycle.
  • Demonstrated ability to coach engineers toward promotion and address underperformance effectively.
  • Experience owning team goals, prioritization, estimation, and delivery.
  • Experience with production on-call, incident response, and capacity planning.
  • Willingness to be actively involved in sourcing, interviewing, and closing engineering talent.

Technical Experience

  • 6+ years of backend software engineering experience in consumer-scale applications.
  • At least 3 years of hands-on Python experience.
  • Experience building and operating machine learning or causal inference systems in production.
  • Earlier-career experience personally building and deploying ML models or ML infrastructure.
  • Ability to participate in technical architecture and system-design discussions and provide technical direction without needing to be the primary coder.
  • Strong understanding of software quality, security, reliability, testing, and production operations.

Technical Skills

We’re particularly interested in candidates with experience across:

  • Languages: Python, SQL
  • Machine Learning: Jupyter, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Docker
  • Streaming: Kafka, Kinesis, Beam, Flink, Spark Streaming
  • Batch Processing: Airflow, Metaflow
  • Databases: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Cassandra, Snowflake, Druid, and/or similar technologies
  • APIs: REST, GraphQL, gRPC, Protocol Buffers
  • Production Engineering: DevOps, SLOs, monitoring/observability, on-call, capacity planning, root-cause analysis
  • ML/Analytics: Machine learning, causal inference, scalable algorithms

Compensation

jobs.title: Engineering Fellowship
jobs.description:
Engineering Fellowship

Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But International Fintechs and non-US banks are left with two unsatisfying options to access it: Either they build on legacy clearing banks that are slow and unreliable, or they interface with middleware providers that don’t move and hold the dollars directly, but themselves rely on underlying legacy banks. Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of operators, unicorn early employees, ex-founders and people who walked away from degrees because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and n8n.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

You’re a Fellow at Augustus, deployed to special projects across engineering, product, and the wider company. You own a project end to end: understand the problem, decide how to approach it, build the solution, and get it into use.

The work depends on where you can have the most impact. You could build background coding agents, create a frontend component library, or solve an operational problem with agents. The common thread is a meaningful problem, a clear outcome, and ownership of getting it done.

You’ll work closely with the team your project sits in. They provide context, technical guidance, and direct feedback. You bring the drive to turn an open-ended problem into something that works. As you deliver, the scope and difficulty of your projects grow.

Your First Months

Get context quickly, ship early, and take on harder problems as you prove yourself.

  • Month 1: Join a team, understand the problem, and take ownership of your first project. Talk to the people who will use what you build, agree on what success looks like, and ship an initial version.

  • Months 2–3: Drive the project through to adoption. Work through technical decisions, collect feedback, and improve the solution. You’re becoming more independent and developing better judgment about where to spend your time.

  • Months 4–6: Take on a larger project or a harder problem, potentially in another team. You can turn an ambiguous brief into a plan, make sound tradeoffs, and deliver with less guidance.

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We care most about your trajectory, drive, and curiosity. You don’t need years of experience. You need evidence that you learn quickly, push yourself, and finish things.

  • Steep trajectory. You’re getting better fast. The problems you can solve today are meaningfully harder than those you could solve six months ago. You seek feedback and put it to work.

  • Drive. You make things happen. You find a way through unfamiliar problems, follow up without being chased, and stay with a project until it works.

  • Curiosity. You want to understand how things work and why. You dig into unfamiliar systems, ask precise questions, and look beyond the first plausible answer.

  • Ownership. You care about the outcome. You involve the right people, raise blockers early, and check that what you shipped actually solves the problem.

  • Low ego. You can defend an idea, change your mind, and commit to a team decision. You care more about getting it right than getting credit.

This fellowship is for you if:

  • You’ve built things outside a course or job because you wanted them to exist.

  • You want an ambitious problem and room to figure it out.

  • You enjoy moving between unfamiliar tools, systems, and domains.

  • You’re willing to do the less exciting work that makes a project useful: testing, documentation, rollout, and iteration.

  • You want direct feedback and responsibility that grows with your ability.

You’ll struggle here if:

  • You need a complete specification before you can start.

  • You’re more interested in starting projects than finishing them.

  • You wait for someone else to notice that you’re blocked.

  • You only want to work within a narrow, predefined remit.

Hard Requirements

  • Available for 3–6 months.

  • Based in Berlin or willing to relocate for an in-person fellowship.

  • Able to build working software, demonstrated through projects, open-source contributions, previous work, or something you can show us.

  • Able to explain your decisions, ask for help when needed, and follow through.

What We Offer

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

  • Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.

  • Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.

  • Perks & Benefits: Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.

Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.

Augustus is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive and where different viewpoints and experiences are valued and respected. Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status.

Compensation: €3K per month

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Experiment Platform, Robot Software
jobs.description:
Engineering Manager, Experiment Platform, Robot Software

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Robot Software builds the on-vehicle software platform that Wayve’s AI Driver runs on. Within it, the Experiment Platform team owns the systems that let our researchers develop driving models on the road: deploying models to vehicles, running experiments, and collecting the data that trains the next model.

The team builds a portable development platform that connects to partner vehicles and brings Wayve’s model development capabilities to them, including data collection, experiment control, telemetry and over-the-air updates. It is used across our own fleet and on pre-production vehicles with OEM partners in Europe and Japan, and is central to how Wayve adapts its AI Driver to new vehicles. You will lead a team of engineers based in London, working alongside the Runtime Platform, OS, Sensors and Platform Integration teams in Robot Software.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You will lead the team’s people, plans and partnerships. Most of your time goes to your engineers: regular 1:1s, clear expectations, feedback, performance and promotion cycles, and helping technical leads take on more scope. You will work with your tech leads on technical decisions, own the outcomes, and make sure the team responds well when issues come up in the field. You will maintain the team’s mission, charter and twelve-month roadmap, turn them into quarterly and six-week plans, and keep delivery on track.

You will be the team’s main point of contact for partner engineering teams, programme managers, operations and OEM customers, and you will make it clear what the team owns.

You will stay technically capable and aware of the team’s work across the codebase. You will monitor the architecture, guide the team through technical blockers when needed, and engage with technical leaders in other teams at a technical level.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

Growing the platform: Take the development platform from its first stable release to a product used across many vehicle types, with predictable releases and validation in CI and on HIL benches.

Experiment control and fleet orchestration: Own model and controller download, the robot state machine, and over-the-air deployment of software, configuration and calibration.

Self-serve experimentation: Make the platform self-serve, so research teams can run their own experiments on vehicles without waiting for platform changes.

Scaling data collection: Onboard and event-based logging, data quality, and data offload over

New vehicles and OEM integrations: Deploy the full platform on Wayve’s next-generation vehicles, and support new OEM integrations through configuration rather than new releases.

Building the operating model around the platform: Releases, support rota, on-call, metrics and observability.

Building the team: Own hiring and onboarding, and grow the team as adoption of the platform expands.

🙌 You should apply if:

You have managed software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching and performance management.

You have owned a platform or product that other teams or customers relied on, and shipped it to devices in the field.

You are technically capable, with hands-on experience in embedded Linux systems software (C++ or Python), and stay close enough to the code to review your team’s work, guide architecture and help resolve technical blockers.

You understand connected device fleets, such as vehicles, robots or IoT, including data logging and offload, over-the-air updates and observability.

You are comfortable leading delivery across many stakeholders, including external partners, and can engage with other technical leaders as a technical peer.

You care about operational reliability and release quality.

Experience with autonomous vehicles or robotics, automotive ECUs (for example NVIDIA Jetson or DRIVE, QNX), Yocto, IPC middleware such as ROS 2 or DDS, or containerised workloads on embedded systems is desirable.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. This role is based in our London office.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

  • Competency Interviews: leadership and management interview, and hiring manager interview; 2 hours total

  • Deep-dive interviews: domain, systems design and code review interviews; 3 hours total

  • Final interview: values alignment (30-45 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

International Expansion

About Us

At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel.

Read more about what we’re building here.

About the role

Axle has quickly become the leader in our operational markets, and we’re now looking to expand our reach internationally.

Our goal is to become the go-to platform for energy flexibility globally, and we’re hiring the person to make that happen.

This role will assess Axle’s future markets and business models from first principles: diving deep into regulations, modelling revenue-per-asset, and trialling new propositions at startup-urgent pace.

What you will be doing

  • High-level strategy development, defining and executing Axle’s international expansion plans, and assessing the commercial value of new markets and business models

  • Diving deep into policy and regulations, understanding how market access works and what needs doing to achieve it

  • Developing the zero-to-one of the business through partnerships with key stakeholders. You’ll be jumping on the phone (and eventually, getting on the ground) with grid operators, utilities/retailers and potential clients to create and disprove hypotheses as quickly as possible.

  • Building the aeroplane as it flies: getting hands dirty with implementation as each international business scales, scoping and setting up pilots, tracking down partners and building relationships.

As such, we are looking for a “full-stack operator” who can process highly technical information, sniff out commercial value, and run through walls to get us into markets at speed.

You might have previous experience in one or more of the activities above, but we are more interested in your growth potential than your domain-specific expertise. We are looking for people who have built things, developed new relationships, and helped get ambitious projects over the line in complex environments.

This is an opportunity to repeatedly deliver first-of-a-kind projects across the world, become a domain expert, and work at the bleeding edge of global electrification.

What's in it for you

A meaningful slice of equity in Axle, alongside a competitive salary, with total compensation ranging from £75k–£200k (base salary + equity).

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Enhanced parental leave to support you through life's meaningful moments.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

Hybrid working - We have a dog-friendly office around Farringdon. To maximize collaboration, we ask that you spend 2-3 days a week in the office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are extremely keen to build a diverse company, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.

  1. Initial interview

  2. Take-home exercise

  3. Final interview (in-person)

  4. Offer, additional references, and welcome to the team!

Compensation: £75K – £200K

  • • Total Compensation (salary + equity) £75K – £200K

Network Customer Support Engineer
jobs.description:
Network Customer Support Engineer

Location: Zurich, Paris or Munich

Language: Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

About Us

Point One Navigation is building the future of precise location. Our mission is to deliver a unified location platform that enables autonomy, safety, and efficiency across industries from robotics to transportation. We are a high-performance, high-collaboration team that thrives on solving complex problems, moving fast, and delivering impact.

Role Outcome

The Network Customer Support Engineer owns the customer support experience tied to the reliability, visibility, and operational health of Point One’s correction network.

This is a player-coach role. You will personally handle complex technical support cases while also leading the operational systems, monitoring, and processes that ensure the network performs reliably at scale.

Success in this role means:

  • Potential customer facing issues are identified and addressed before they impact customers.

  • When incidents do occur, they are resolved quickly with clear communication and strong root-cause analysis.

  • The organization has clear visibility into network health, operational trends, and customer friction.

  • A scalable network operations and support function is built as the company and network footprint grow.

Immediate Areas of Focus

Own the customer experience of our Network

  • Work with our Network Operations team to understand incidents that affect the customer experience

  • Identify emerging issues and collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to understand and support the resolution of those issues.

  • Understand available metrics and dashboards and contribute to the development of these tools to allow for the targeted resolution of customer questions.

Deliver High-Quality Technical Support

  • Liaison between Engineering, Network Operations and FAE and FDE team to support the customer.

  • Personally manage high-impact or technically complex support cases.

  • Partner closely with FAEs, Product, and Engineering to diagnose issues and close the loop with customers.

  • Ensure customers receive clear, confident communication during investigations and incidents.

  • Model best-in-class technical troubleshooting and customer engagement practices for the team.

Build the Foundation for a Scalable Operations & Support Function

  • Design and implement systems that enable both network operations and customer support to scale.

  • Define a support ticket taxonomy that reflects customer use cases, technical complexity, and operational impact.

  • Support Network Ops team on operational metrics such as:

    • Network uptime and availability

    • Incident response and resolution times

    • Support response and resolution times

    • Alert quality and monitoring coverage

    • Document operational procedures, escalation paths, and ownership models.

  • Develop automation and tooling to reduce manual work and improve operational efficiency.

Surface Operational and Customer Insights

  • Identify patterns across support tickets, network events, and operational data.

  • Translate operational signals into actionable insights for Product and Engineering.

  • Ensure recurring issues and infrastructure gaps are clearly surfaced and prioritized.

  • Create lightweight reporting that gives leadership visibility into network reliability, operational trends, and customer friction.

Establish Visibility Into Customer Experience

  • Define and implement the right metrics for understanding customer experience and operational impact.

  • Establish mechanisms to collect structured customer feedback without creating noise.

  • Use both operational data and customer feedback to drive continuous improvement.

Coach and Develop the Operations & Support Function

  • Act as a player-coach, leading through hands-on operational work while building the foundations of the team.

  • Train and mentor support engineers on troubleshooting methodology, operational awareness, and customer communication.

  • Establish clear expectations for technical depth, ownership, and responsiveness.

  • Continuously raise the operational and support bar as the team grows.

Qualifications

  • Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

  • Experience in a player-coach technical operations or support role where you owned both hands-on troubleshooting and operational systems.

  • Strong technical background in GPS/GNSS, precise localization, geospatial infrastructure, or closely related domains (robotics, autonomy, embedded systems, positioning technologies).

  • Experience operating or supporting distributed infrastructure or network-based systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to build or significantly improve monitoring, alerting, and operational processes.

  • Proven experience troubleshooting complex technical systems and working directly with customers.

  • Experience conducting incident response and root cause analysis.

  • Ability to define metrics, processes, and documentation without over-engineering.

  • Comfort working cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, and Go-To-Market teams in a fast-moving environment.

  • Bias toward ownership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Our Cultural Foundation

At Point One, our cultural and operating design is built around one guiding principle: we must move with extreme speed and efficiency of effort to stay in a leadership position.

This environment gives people a high level of autonomy and the ability to make a real impact. It also challenges every team member to grow — both professionally and personally. Because we focus on promoting from within rather than relying on external hiring, the opportunities for advancement are tremendous for those who seek them.

That said, growth only comes from delivering in the present. What matters most is the job to be done today, not the job you want tomorrow. When we all focus on today’s outcomes with excellence, the path to greater responsibility and growth naturally follows.

We think about our culture in two dimensions:

How We Show Up Every Day

These are the behaviors we expect every team member to bring to work — the foundation of being a consummate, high-output teammate:

  • Trust / Assume Best Intent — Trust allows us to move fast. When we start from trust, we spend no time second-guessing or looking for ulterior motives and thus focus all our energy on acting.

  • High Output, Action Oriented — Our default posture is “yes.” We bias toward action and deliver results quickly, knowing that speed and efficiency compound into impact as we unblock others around us.

  • Divine Discontent — We’re never satisfied with the status quo and are self-motivated to improve ourselves, our work, and our company. We actively seek feedback in real-time to shorten improvement cycles.

  • No Ego, One Team — Collaboration without ego creates leverage. When we win as one team, we eliminate friction and move faster together.

  • Self Accountability — Taking ownership is the straightest line to learning, self-improvement, and correcting our course of action. And blaming others around us is a fast path to destroying trust.

Operating Principles

These are the systems and norms that amplify speed and efficiency at the company level:

  • Edge Innovation — We bias toward action over approval. Experiment, decide, and move — failure is just a step toward faster learning.

  • No Hierarchies — We practice self-prioritization and go direct to the source. Flattening layers reduces drag and maximizes autonomy.

  • Customer Experience First — We optimize for the end-to-end customer outcome, not functional or departmental efficiency. This focus cuts waste, aligns priorities, and ensures we spend effort where it matters most.

If this role sounds like a fit, we’d love to hear from you. Apply below and join us in shaping the future of precise location.

jobs.title: Scientific Account Executive
jobs.description:
Scientific Account Executive

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers — from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

The day-to-day:

  • Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

  • Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

  • Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

  • Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

  • Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts — new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.

  • Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).

  • Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.

  • Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.

  • Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.

  • Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.

  • Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

What we're looking for

  • Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.

  • Self-starter who can manage their own pipeline and priorities without heavy oversight.

  • Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

jobs.title: Bioengineer, Display & Library Engineering
jobs.description:
Bioengineer, Display & Library Engineering

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You are here to scale up data generation. Design teams can hand us 10⁶ sequences, and our automated infrastructure measures on the order of 10³ of them individually. Library construction and display is what closes that gap.

We want someone who has set these systems up before and can do it again here, with their own hands. Phage, ribosome, mRNA, yeast, cell-free: which one fits depends on the library and the target, and part of the job is making that call and then building it rather than writing a recommendation.

This is a build role, not a service role. For your first months you are making libraries, running selections, working out why a round collapsed, and turning what works into something the automation team can run without you.

What You'll Do

  • Build the libraries. Oligo pools, combinatorial assembly, barcoding. More campaigns fail here than at selection.

  • Run selections end to end, including the call on whether a round enriched real binders or just fast growers.

  • Pick the platform per campaign and stand it up. Based on the library and the target, not on what you happened to use last.

  • Own the sequencing analysis. You don't need to be a bioinformatician, but you can't be waiting on one.

  • Hand off to automation. A protocol that only works when you personally run it isn't finished.

  • Close the loop. Selected designs get expressed and measured on BLI and SPR by the team next door. That tells you whether the selection worked.

What We're Looking For

  • MSc / PhD in molecular biology, protein engineering, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years running display and selection yourself.

  • You have set up a display platform, not just used one. This is the core requirement. Built the library, got the selection working, and produced binders that held up in an independent assay. Managing outsourced CRO campaigns is not the same thing.

  • Depth in at least one display format and working literacy across the rest. We are not fixed on which one.

  • High-diversity cloning, and an understanding of where bias enters a pool and what it costs you later.

  • NGS as a routine tool, and FACS if you have it.

  • Enough Python or R to analyze your own data without joining a queue.

  • You use AI tools seriously. It's 2026 and we run on Claude Code across the company. You also need the judgment to check what comes back.

  • A self-starter. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue. You decide what to build, build it, and tell us what you learned.

  • Startup speed, not academic pace. Campaigns run against customer deadlines. A working platform with known limits beats an elegant one next year.

  • You want your protocols automated rather than manual forever.

If your instinct is that a campaign is finished once you have ten good clones, we will frustrate each other. We want data, not a hit list.

  • Type: Full time

  • Start date: ASAP

Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid, denkt vooruit en voelt je op je plek in een omgeving die continu in beweging is.

Je herkent jezelf in het volgende:

  • Je hebt een afgeronde opleiding in bijvoorbeeld Electrical Engineering, Industriële Automatisering, Informatica of een vergelijkbare richting.

  • Je hebt minimaal 4 jaar ervaring met Operational Technology (OT), industriële automatisering of industriële besturingssystemen, waarvan een deel gericht is op cybersecurity of OT-beveiliging.

  • Je hebt ervaring met industriële omgevingen zoals de chemische industrie, procesindustrie, energie- of raffinagesector.

  • Je hebt kennis van industriële besturingssystemen zoals DCS-, PLC-, SCADA- en HMI-omgevingen.

  • Je hebt ervaring met OT-netwerken en industriële protocollen zoals Ethernet/IP, Modbus TCP, OPC UA, PROFINET of PROFIBUS.

  • Je begrijpt hoe beschikbaarheid, betrouwbaarheid, veiligheid en cybersecurity elkaar beïnvloeden binnen een productieomgeving.

  • Je bent in staat technische problemen te analyseren over verschillende disciplines heen, zoals software, netwerken en industriële apparatuur.

  • Je hebt ervaring met infrastructuurcomponenten zoals virtualisatieplatformen, Active Directory en DNS.

  • Je spreekt en schrijft vloeiend Nederlands en Engels.

Nice to have:

  • Ervaring met IEC 62443, NIS2 of andere relevante cybersecuritystandaarden voor industriële omgevingen.

  • Ervaring met greenfieldprojecten, commissioning of de ingebruikname van nieuwe installaties.

  • Ervaring met OT-monitoring- en asset visibility-platformen zoals Claroty, Nozomi, Dragos of vergelijkbare oplossingen.

  • Kennis van functionele veiligheid, Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS) en IEC 61511.

  • Certificeringen zoals GICSP, ISA/IEC 62443, CISSP of vergelijkbaar.

Over DSL-01

In Delfzijl bouwen we aan DSL-01, een fabriek van SkyNRG voor hernieuwbare brandstoffen. Hier produceren we Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) uit reststromen zoals gebruikte vetten en oliën, met HEFA-technologie. Daarnaast maken we bijproducten zoals butaan, propaan en nafta.

DSL-01 wordt de eerste fabriek in Europa die volledig gericht is op SAF en bijbehorende duurzame bijproducten. Als de fabriek in bedrijf is, produceren we jaarlijks 100.000 ton SAF en 35.000 ton bijproducten. Daarmee verminderen we de uitstoot van broeikasgassen met circa 80% ten opzichte van fossiele kerosine, gemeten over de hele keten.

De bouw is gestart in 2026 en de eerste productie staat gepland voor 2028. Het project omvat de fabriek zelf, bijbehorende leidingen en tijdelijke werkterreinen. Je draagt direct bij aan de realisatie van een nieuwe industriële fabriek en de verduurzaming van de luchtvaart.

We werken volgens internationale standaarden en Nederlandse wet- en regelgeving om de impact op mens, natuur en omgeving zorgvuldig te beheersen. Veiligheid, duurzaamheid en samenwerking staan daarbij centraal.


Wat wij bieden

DSL-01 is volop in ontwikkeling. Dat geldt niet alleen voor de fabriek, maar ook voor de organisatie en de arbeidsvoorwaarden. Ons HR-team werkt aan een passend en marktconform pakket voor de locatie in Delfzijl.

Je kunt rekenen op een goed salaris, een bonusregeling en arbeidsvoorwaarden die ruimte bieden voor jouw professionele en persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Wil jij meebouwen aan een nieuwe fabriek en het resultaat van je werk terugzien in de praktijk? Dan is dit je kans om bij te dragen aan de ontwikkeling van duurzame luchtvaart.

Meer weten over DSL-01 en SkyNRG? Kijk op www.skynrg.com.

SkyNRG is een werkgever die gelijke kansen biedt. Senior Software Enginner (Full-stack Node + React)

About us:

Airtm is a financial-infrastructure company building the future of the online-work economy. We are on a mission to empower the world's growing number of Digital Entrepreneurs in the Global South, giving them the financial freedom to thrive.

The problem is clear: in emerging markets, accessing the dollar economy is difficult. Cross-border payments are slow, expensive, and often lose value to inflation. This limits the potential of millions of talented individuals.

Airtm’s solution is a swift and comprehensive financial platform that facilitates low-value cross-border payments and local cash-outs. As pioneers in stablecoin-payment infrastructure, Airtm has built the most advanced cross-border payment system available on the market.

As a company married to the world of online work, Airtm will go beyond payments to build the necessary infrastructure the online-work economy needs to thrive. We are fostering an entirely new economy, giving individuals, communities, and countries the tools to take control of their financial destinies.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to design, build, and evolve the full stack systems that power Airtm’s financial products. You’ll work within one of our autonomous product pods, taking ownership of projects end-to-end, from technical design through production, and mentoring the engineers around you.

Our stack is TypeScript/Node.js microservices deployed on Kubernetes, paired with React front ends. You’ll work across the entire stack, backend and frontend, as needed to deliver on your pod’s goals, collaborating with engineers in other pods when initiatives cross boundaries. AI-assisted development is core to how we build software: you’ll be expected to use AI coding tools fluently to move faster without sacrificing quality.

Key Responsibilities

  • Technical Design: Lead the design of medium-to-large features across the stack, document decisions, and anticipate edge cases and long-term maintainability
  • Full Stack Development: Build and maintain TypeScript/Node.js microservices, event handlers, and cronjobs, as well as the React UIs that consume them, powering our core financial flows
  • AI-Assisted Development: Use AI coding assistants and agentic tools as part of your daily workflow, from scaffolding and refactoring to test generation and code review, while maintaining a high bar for correctness and judgment about when and how much to rely on them
  • Project Ownership: Break down complex problems into actionable work across multiple services and UIs; drive delivery from design through deployment
  • Code Quality: Write well-tested, maintainable code; conduct thorough code reviews (including AI-generated code) and hold a high bar for the team
  • Mentorship: Mentor junior and mid-level engineers, including on effective and responsible use of AI tooling; share knowledge and elevate the team’s technical practices
  • Cross-Pod Collaboration: Coordinate with engineers in other pods when work crosses service boundaries; contribute code to shared services following established ownership guidelines
  • On-Call: Participate in on-call rotation for services the pod owns; lead incident response and post-incident reviews
  • Technical Debt: Proactively identify and address technical debt; balance short-term delivery with long-term health of the systems

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with demonstrated full stack range (backend services and frontend UIs)
  • Proficiency in TypeScript and Node.js for building production services
  • Proficiency in React for building production-facing UIs (state management, component design, performance)
  • Experience designing and building REST or GraphQL APIs
  • Solid understanding of relational databases (PostgreSQL or similar), modeling, query optimization, and migrations
  • Familiarity with event-driven architecture and messaging patterns (Kafka, SQS, or similar)
  • Experience working in a microservices environment
  • Hands-on, day-to-day experience with AI-assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, Zed’s Agentic editing, or similar) for coding, debugging, and code review; comfort with prompt/context engineering and sound judgment about validating AI-generated output
  • Strong grasp of software design principles: separation of concerns, error handling, testing strategies
  • Experience writing unit, integration, and end-to-end tests
  • Comfort operating in a cloud environment (AWS preferred), understanding of deployments, logs, and basic infrastructure concepts
  • Strong communication skills; proactive about sharing progress, blockers, and technical risks

Nice to Have

  • Experience building or integrating AI/LLM-powered features into products (RAG, agents, tool calling, prompt pipelines)
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes and container-based deployments
  • Background in fintech, payments, or financial systems
  • Experience working with GraphQL (schema design, federation, or tooling)
  • Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines (Bitbucket Pipelines, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD)
  • Familiarity with observability tooling (Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana)
  • Experience mentoring engineers or leading technical design discussions

What We Look For

Beyond the technical skills, we’re looking for engineers who:

  • Take ownership, they drive their work to completion and communicate early when something is at risk
  • Write code for the next engineer, clean, tested, and documented, whether they or an AI tool wrote the first draft
  • Improve the team around them, through reviews, mentorship, and knowledge sharing
  • Collaborate across boundaries, they engage other pods constructively when work crosses service lines
  • Have good technical judgment, they balance pragmatism with quality, know when to push back on scope, and know when (and when not) to lean on AI tooling

Compensation

Additional Information

Graphene Photonics Device Reliability Testing Engineer (f/m/d)

About us

We see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision. The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects

About our technology

The semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks. The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude

In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution

 

The Role

We are seeking a Device Reliability Testing Engineer to drive reliability qualification, failure analysis, and accelerated life testing for our integrated graphene photonics products. In close collaboration with Design Enablement, Process Integration, and Product Quality, you will establish robust test methodologies to validate device reliability, and long-term stability in accordance with industry standards.

You will play a key role in transitioning our technology from prototype to production- qualified products, ensuring that graphene photonics meet the performance and robustness requirements of high-volume deployment.

To join our team, you should be excited to:

  • Design and execute wafer-level device reliability test plans for graphene- based photonic devices (DC bias, RF endurance, thermal cycling, long-term stability)

  • Identify and investigate the physical mechanisms of graphene-related failure modes.

  • Characterize and monitor key performance metrics, including extinction ratio, insertion loss, bandwidth retention, energy efficiency, dark current stability, responsivity degradation over device lifetime

  • Drive structured root cause investigations using FMEA/8D methodologies and feed findings back to Design and Process teams

  • Work together with product and quality teams to reach compliance with industry standards (JEDEC, OIF, IEC, IEEE) and generate qualification and reliability documentation

Your Qualifications

  • Ph.D. or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, or Photonics Engineering

  • Hands-on experience in semiconductor device physics, optoelectronics, or reliability engineering

  • Hands-on experience in photonic device characterization and reliability testing

  • Experience with high-speed RF testing (>40 GHz) and VNA-based S- parameter measurements.

  • Experience with advanced test equipment such as VNA, real-time and sampling oscilloscopes (50+ GHz), lightwave component analyzers (LCA), optical spectrum analyzers, and probe stations.

Our work culture

People Over Processes. At Black Semiconductor, flexibility is key—we ensure work adapts to life, not the other way around. We champion work-life harmony, where careers are meaningful and enriching. Our processes are human-centric, allowing you to focus on what matters

Your Health and Future Matter. Your well-being is paramount. We offer a comprehensive benefits package with outstanding insurance, pension and virtual stock options for your mental, physical, and financial health. Your peace of mind is our priority - in the present and future

We Live Openness. Collaboration and inclusivity are the cornerstones of our culture. We practice openness, fostering trust and respect. Individuality is our collective strength, fueling innovation and driving us forward

We connect chips – and people. We encourage qualified individuals from any background to apply. We foster an inclusive and supportive work environment that values collaboration, innovation, and growth. Join our team and be part of an organization dedicated to making a difference in the industry

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Synthetic Organic Chemistry
jobs.description:
Research Scientist, Synthetic Organic Chemistry

About us

We're reverse-engineering the origin of life — one of the great unsolved problems in science, and one we think AI finally makes tractable. Understanding this transition, from geochemistry to biochemistry, is what will let us orchestrate molecular networks and build systems that are more capable, adaptive, and efficient.

If we succeed, the applications are vast: catalysis, green synthesis, ab initio synthetic biology, programmable matter. Understanding and harnessing these processes could let ten billion of us thrive on this planet — and let life keep evolving beyond it.

We're a small, diverse team of AI engineers, computational scientists, and bench scientists. We hold ourselves to the rigor of a research institute, but we ship like an engineering firm. Global team, HQs in Cambridge, MA and London, UK.

The role

We're looking for a chemist who combines organic synthesis with strong analytical expertise. You'll synthesise biological molecules — including peptides, nucleic acid derivatives, and modified building blocks — and develop methods to understand how they behave in chemical and biochemical reactions.

Analytical method development is a central part of the role. You'll use chromatography and mass spectrometry to identify products, quantify reaction progress, and resolve complex mixtures. Working closely with our enzymologists and computational scientists, you'll help decide what to make, how to measure it, and what the results tell us about the underlying chemistry.

What you'll do

  • Design and execute syntheses of biological molecules and their derivatives, optimising reaction conditions and purification strategies.

  • Develop and troubleshoot LC-MS/MS methods, particularly triple-quadrupole methods for targeted quantification of substrates and products.

  • Apply Orbitrap-based proteomics workflows to characterise peptides, proteins, and their modifications.

  • Establish compound identity and purity using chromatography, NMR, and mass spectrometry.

  • Work with experimental and computational colleagues to design assays, test proposed chemistry, and investigate unexpected results.

  • Build reproducible synthetic and analytical workflows, with appropriate controls, calibration, and clear documentation.

Essential experience

We're interested in what you've made and measured, and how you approached the chemistry. We care about:

  • Practical experience in organic synthesis of biological molecules, particularly peptides and/or nucleic acid derivatives.

  • Strong analytical method development skills, including sample preparation, chromatographic separation, and quantitative mass spectrometry.

  • Hands-on experience with triple-quadrupole LC-MS/MS and Orbitrap-based proteomics.

  • The ability to independently troubleshoot synthetic and analytical problems, from poor reaction yields to ambiguous spectra or matrix effects.

  • Sound scientific judgement about experimental design, data quality, and what your measurements can support.

Highly preferred

  • Experience with solid-phase peptide or oligonucleotide synthesis, bioconjugation, or non-canonical building blocks.

  • Familiarity with acoustic ejection technologies for sample handling or mass spectrometry.

  • Experience developing high-throughput analytical workflows or integrating methods with laboratory automation.

  • Experience characterising enzyme-catalysed reactions or working closely with chemical biologists and enzymologists.

Logistics

Compensation is highly competitive. We're also able to sponsor visas for the right candidate.
